answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits prove it made a false claim or double-spent. To earn trust, an agent must build a history of valid work before its bond unlocks, so creating many fresh identities does not instantly multiply influence. A sybil attacker must lock up capital in every persona and risk losing it; spreading identities also cannot cheaply evade penalties tied to the same controlling wallet. Even an oasis of new accounts offers no free pearl: each must pay the same costly pigment of collateral.
